children: will acquire LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million, giving the US drugmaker a foothold in Huntington's disease, an area where no disease-modifying therapies have yet been approved.

Cambridge, England-based LoQus23 said on Monday the all-cash deal will include upfront and milestone payments. The privately held biotech firm is developing small-molecule therapies for Huntington's disease and related genetic disorders.
LoQus23's lead candidate, LQT-23, is a potential first-in-class oral inhibitor of MSH3, a protein involved in DNA mismatch repair linked to the progression of Huntington's disease
The company said it expects to submit a clinical trial application for LQT-23 in the near future
Huntington's disease is an inherited, progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which nerve cells in the brain break down over time, leading to movement, cognitive, and mood problems
The condition affects approximately 41,000 people in the US, LoQus23 said
Earlier this month, Dutch gene therapy developer uniQure
said that the US FDA had accepted its application for a Huntington's disease treatment and would decide on the drug by May next year
In preclinical studies, LQT-23 blocked somatic expansion in Huntington's disease cellular systems and animal models
LoQus23 was founded in 2019 with seed funding from SV Health Investors’ Dementia Discovery Fund
